concepts.def: The unit in which chemical amounts are measured; the symbol for the unit mole is mol. A label such as '0.50 mol of sodium chloride' states a chemical amount, not a mass and not a volume.
The mass of one mole of a substance in grams is numerically equal to its relative formula mass. One mole of CaCO₃ (Mr = 100) has a mass of 100 g; one mole of H₂O (Mr = 18) has a mass of 18 g.

concepts.term: Equal amounts, equal numbers of particles
concepts.def: One mole of a substance contains the same number of the stated particles - atoms, molecules or ions - as one mole of any other substance. Equal amounts in moles therefore mean equal numbers of particles, however different the masses are.
The number of atoms, molecules or ions in a mole of a given substance. Its value is 6.02 x 10²³ per mole. It is a number of particles per mole, not per gram.

Amounts in moles can be applied to atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, formulae and equations. In one mole of carbon (C) the number of atoms is the same as the number of molecules in one mole of carbon dioxide (CO₂), although one mole of CO₂ contains three moles of atoms.
The number of moles in a given mass is found by dividing that mass in grams by the relative formula mass: number of moles = mass ÷ Mr. 20 g of CaCO₃ (Mr = 100) is 0.20 mol.
The mass of a known amount is found by multiplying the amount in moles by the relative formula mass: mass = number of moles x Mr. 0.25 mol of MgCl₂ (Mr = 95) has a mass of 23.75 g.
The masses of reactants and products can be calculated from balanced symbol equations. In a closed system the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants that reacted.

Chemical equations can be interpreted in terms of moles. Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ shows that one mole of magnesium reacts with two moles of hydrochloric acid to produce one mole of magnesium chloride and one mole of hydrogen gas.

The balancing numbers in an equation give the ratio of the amounts in moles of the substances involved. They do not give the ratio of the masses, because each substance has its own relative formula mass.

To find the mass of one substance from the mass of another: convert the known mass to moles using its Mr, apply the mole ratio from the balanced equation, then convert back to a mass using the Mr of the substance wanted.

The balancing numbers in a symbol equation can be calculated from the masses of reactants and products by converting the masses in grams to amounts in moles and converting the numbers of moles to simple whole number ratios.

The amounts in moles are divided through by the smallest of them, and multiplied up if needed, so that the balancing numbers are the simplest whole numbers that fit. 0.2 : 0.1 : 0.2 becomes 2 : 1 : 2.
A relationship can be rearranged to make any of its quantities the subject. From number of moles = mass ÷ Mr come mass = number of moles x Mr and Mr = mass ÷ number of moles.
A reactant supplied in more than the amount the equation requires. Using an excess of one reactant makes sure that all of the other reactant is used up.

The reactant that is completely used up in a reaction. It is called the limiting reactant because it limits the amount of products: the amount of product is worked out from the amount of the limiting reactant, not from the reactant in excess.

mcqs.q: A bottle in a laboratory is labelled '0.50 mol of sodium chloride'. What does the '0.50 mol' tell you?
options: the chemical amount of sodium chloride present
the mass of the sodium chloride, in grams
the number of sodium ions in the bottle
the volume the sodium chloride fills
mcqs.explain: Chemical amounts are measured in moles and mol is the symbol for that unit, so the label states an amount of substance.

mcqs.q: The relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, is 100. What is the mass of one mole of calcium carbonate?
options: 1 g
mcqs.explain: The mass of one mole in grams is numerically equal to the relative formula mass, so one mole of CaCO₃ has a mass of 100 g.

mcqs.q: One mole of water, H₂O (Mr = 18), has a smaller mass than one mole of sulfur dioxide, SO₂ (Mr = 64). Why?
options: water is a liquid while sulfur dioxide is a gas
one mole of water contains fewer molecules
the relative formula mass of water is smaller
water molecules are packed more closely
mcqs.explain: The mass of one mole in grams is numerically equal to the relative formula mass, and 18 is less than 64.

mcqs.q: A sample holds one mole of magnesium atoms. Another sample holds one mole of helium atoms. Which statement is correct?
options: The magnesium sample contains more atoms than the helium.
The helium sample contains more atoms, as it is lighter.
The two samples must have the same mass as each other.
The two samples contain the same number of atoms.
mcqs.explain: One mole of a substance contains the same number of the stated particles as one mole of any other substance.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the Avogadro constant?
options: 6.02 x 10²³ particles in one mole
6.02 x 10²² particles in a mole
6.02 x 10²³ particles per gram
6.02 x 10²³ g for every mole
mcqs.explain: The number of atoms, molecules or ions in a mole of a given substance is 6.02 x 10²³ per mole.

mcqs.q: What does the Avogadro constant tell you?
options: the number of particles in one gram of any substance
the number of particles in one mole of a substance
the number of moles in one gram of a substance
the mass in grams of one mole of a substance
mcqs.explain: The number of atoms, molecules or ions in a mole of a given substance is the Avogadro constant.

mcqs.q: In one mole of carbon (C) the number of atoms is the same as the number of molecules in one mole of carbon dioxide (CO₂). How many moles of atoms are there in one mole of CO₂?
options: one mole of atoms, as this is one mole of substance
44 moles of atoms, from its relative formula mass
three moles of atoms, one carbon and two oxygen
two moles of atoms, one for each element present
mcqs.explain: Each CO₂ molecule holds three atoms, so one mole of molecules contains three moles of atoms.

mcqs.q: Which statement about amounts in moles is correct?
options: One mole of any solid contains 6.02 x 10²³ atoms.
Moles can count atoms but not electrons or ions.
One mole of CO₂ contains one mole of atoms in total.
One mole of MgCl₂ contains three moles of ions.
mcqs.explain: Amounts in moles apply to ions as well as atoms and molecules: one mole of MgCl₂ gives one mole of Mg²⁺ and two moles of Cl⁻.

mcqs.q: How many moles are there in 20 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃ (Mr = 100)?
options: 0.20 mol
5.0 mol
20 mol
2 mol
mcqs.explain: number of moles = mass ÷ Mr = 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20 mol.

mcqs.q: What is the mass of 0.25 mol of magnesium chloride, MgCl₂ (Mr = 95)?
mcqs.explain: mass = number of moles x Mr = 0.25 x 95 = 23.75 g.

mcqs.q: Magnesium burns in oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. In a sealed container, 4.8 g of magnesium reacts completely with 3.2 g of oxygen. Which statement about the magnesium oxide formed is correct?
options: It is less than 8.0 g, as some mass is lost as gas.
It is 4.8 g, since only the magnesium is weighed out.
It is 8.0 g, the total mass of the reactants.
It is 3.2 g, the mass of the oxygen that reacted.
mcqs.explain: Mass is conserved in a closed system, so 4.8 g + 3.2 g of reactants give 8.0 g of magnesium oxide.

mcqs.q: The equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O can be interpreted in terms of moles. Which reading of it is correct?
options: Two grams of H₂ react with one gram of O₂ gas.
H₂ and O₂ react in a 2 : 1 ratio by mass.
Two molecules of H₂ give one molecule of H₂O.
Two moles of H₂ react with one mole of O₂.
mcqs.explain: The balancing numbers give the amounts in moles: two moles of hydrogen to one mole of oxygen.

mcqs.q: The equation Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ is given in the specification. Which statement does it show?
options: One mole of Mg reacts with two moles of HCl.
A gram of Mg reacts with two grams of HCl.
The masses of Mg and HCl are in a 1 : 2 ratio.
One mole of Mg needs two grams of HCl.
mcqs.explain: The balancing numbers show one mole of magnesium reacting with two moles of hydrochloric acid.

mcqs.q: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. What mass of magnesium chloride (Mr = 95) is produced when 2.4 g of magnesium (Ar = 24) reacts completely?
mcqs.explain: 2.4 ÷ 24 = 0.1 mol of Mg, which gives 0.1 mol of MgCl₂, and 0.1 x 95 = 9.5 g.

mcqs.q: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. What mass of calcium oxide (Mr = 56) is produced when 25 g of calcium carbonate (Mr = 100) decomposes completely?
mcqs.explain: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 mol of CaCO₃ gives 0.25 mol of CaO, and 0.25 x 56 = 14 g.

mcqs.q: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. What mass of calcium carbonate (Mr = 100) must be heated to produce 5.6 g of calcium oxide (Mr = 56)?
mcqs.explain: 5.6 ÷ 56 = 0.1 mol of CaO, so 0.1 mol of CaCO₃ is needed, and 0.1 x 100 = 10 g.

mcqs.q: In N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, one mole of nitrogen reacts with three moles of hydrogen. Why is the mass of hydrogen used not three times the mass of nitrogen?
options: the balancing numbers give a ratio of moles, not of masses
the mass ratio is the same as the mole ratio in all cases
some of the hydrogen escapes before it is able to react
hydrogen must have more mass, as it has more molecules
mcqs.explain: Each amount must be converted to a mass using its own relative formula mass, so the mass ratio is 6 g to 28 g.

mcqs.q: The masses of the reactants and products in a reaction are known. How are the balancing numbers in the symbol equation found?
options: use the ratio of the masses in grams as the numbers
convert each mass to moles, then find the simplest ratio
divide each mass by the first element's relative atomic mass
multiply each mass by its relative formula mass
mcqs.explain: Masses in grams are converted to amounts in moles, and those amounts are converted to simple whole number ratios.

mcqs.q: 4.0 g of hydrogen (Mr of H₂ = 2), 32 g of oxygen (Mr of O₂ = 32) and 36 g of water (Mr of H₂O = 18) are measured in a reaction. Which balanced equation fits these masses?
options: 4H₂ + 2O₂ → 4H₂O
4H₂ + 32O₂ → 36H₂O
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
H₂ + O₂ → H₂O
mcqs.explain: 4.0 ÷ 2 = 2 mol H₂, 32 ÷ 32 = 1 mol O₂ and 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol H₂O, a ratio of 2 : 1 : 2.

mcqs.q: 2.4 g of magnesium (Ar = 24) reacts with 7.3 g of hydrochloric acid (Mr of HCl = 36.5) to give 9.5 g of magnesium chloride (Mr = 95) and 0.2 g of hydrogen (Mr of H₂ = 2). Which equation fits these masses?
options: 2Mg + 4HCl → 2MgCl₂ + 2H₂
2.4Mg + 7.3HCl → 9.5MgCl₂ + 0.2H₂
Mg + HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
mcqs.explain: 0.1 mol Mg, 0.2 mol HCl, 0.1 mol MgCl₂ and 0.1 mol H₂ give the ratio 1 : 2 : 1 : 1.

mcqs.q: The amount of a substance is found from number of moles = mass ÷ Mr. To make mass the subject of this relationship, what should you do?
options: Multiply the number of moles by the Mr.
Multiply the mass by the number of moles.
Divide the Mr by the number of moles.
Divide the number of moles by Mr.
mcqs.explain: Multiplying both sides by Mr leaves mass on its own, giving mass = number of moles x Mr.

mcqs.q: Concentration = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution. A student knows the concentration and the volume and needs the mass of solute. What should they do?
options: Multiply the concentration by 1000 cm³ first.
Multiply the concentration by the volume.
Divide the concentration by the volume used.
Divide the volume by the concentration.
mcqs.explain: Multiplying both sides by the volume makes the mass of solute the subject.

mcqs.q: In a reaction between two reactants, what is meant by the limiting reactant?
options: the reactant that is added in excess
the reactant with the smallest mass used
the reactant that is completely used up
the reactant that is left over at the end
mcqs.explain: The reactant that is completely used up is called the limiting reactant because it limits the amount of products.

mcqs.q: Magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. A student adds 0.10 mol of magnesium to 0.10 mol of hydrochloric acid. Which statement is correct?
options: The magnesium is limiting, as it has the smaller mass.
Neither reactant is limiting, as the amounts match.
The magnesium is the limiting reactant in this mixture.
The hydrochloric acid is the limiting reactant.
mcqs.explain: 0.10 mol of Mg needs 0.20 mol of HCl, so the acid runs out first and the magnesium is in excess.

mcqs.q: In 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, 0.20 mol of magnesium is burned in 0.50 mol of oxygen. Which statement is correct?
options: 0.20 mol of MgO forms, as the magnesium is limiting
0.50 mol of MgO forms, since the oxygen is in excess
2 mol of MgO forms, straight from the equation
0.10 mol of MgO forms, from the 2 in the equation
mcqs.explain: 0.20 mol of Mg needs only 0.10 mol of O₂, so the magnesium is used up and gives 0.20 mol of MgO.

mcqs.q: A reaction is repeated with twice as much of the limiting reactant, while the other reactant is still in excess. What happens to the maximum mass of product?
options: It stays the same, as the equation fixes the amount formed.
It doubles, as the limiting reactant sets the amount formed.
It halves, because the excess reactant is now shared out.
It is unchanged until the excess reactant is doubled.
mcqs.explain: The amount of product is proportional to the amount of the limiting reactant while the other is in excess.
